meta.title: Docs: the contract, the loop, Recall, budgets · Fizlet
meta.description: How Fizlet's kernel and bricks work: getting started, the nine-rule contract, the loop, Recall, size budgets and determinism, with numbers from v0.27.0.

head.lead: Fizlet is the building blocks for animation and games on the DOM: a small kernel and bricks, so a piece boils down to logic and style. Start with the five-minute setup, then the ideas everything else rests on: the contract, the loop, Recall, the budgets and determinism. Every brick's API is in Bricks.

cards.label: Getting started
cards.body: Load Fizlet with one script tag or only the modules you need, start an engine, and give the page back with destroy().

cards.label: Authoring and recipes
cards.body: How every Fizlet piece is written, the bricks to pick for each use, and three recipes that run on the page: an action, a shooter and two players.

cards.label: The contract
cards.body: The nine rules every brick and every game on Fizlet keeps, and the test that proves each one.

cards.label: The loop
cards.body: One shared requestAnimationFrame, a fixed 60 Hz step with a catch-up cap, three phases, auto-pause, settle and the fps cap.

cards.label: Recall and the ledger
cards.body: Every page change goes through one ledger: change-only writes, exact restore, and a newer host edit always wins.

cards.label: Size budgets
cards.body: Every module has a gzip budget checked in CI. The table is measured on the build you are reading.

cards.label: Determinism
cards.body: A fixed step, a seeded random and state in typed arrays: runs replay, peers stay in lockstep, and syncCheck proves it.

map.note: Every module, its API and its size.
